sections.name: Bowser Space (Bowser's roulette)
sections.card:
Summary: A board space that calls up Bowser to take your coins. Mario Party's first game has you spin a roulette that picks one event, from a plain coin fine to a minigame where the losers pay him.
Weak points: Winning a Bowser minigame only helps in part. In Bowser Balloon Burst everyone except the winner pays Bowser; in Face Lift only those who score under 90 do; in Tug o' War the side that loses does. Exceptions: a tie in Balloon Burst or Tug o' War costs every player 10 to 50 coins. If all four players reach 90 in Face Lift, Bowser takes up to 50 coins off the one who landed. In Bash 'n' Cash the one who landed wears the Bowser Suit: coins knocked out of them go to Bowser, and if they lose none he takes 15 from them.
Tips: The Coins for Bowser event costs the player who landed 10 to 50 coins. Bowser Revolution gathers everyone's coins and shares them out in equal parts. In Bowser's Chance Time the coins always go to Bowser. The wheel also shows Star Steal, 100 Star Present and 1000 Coin Present in yellow text, but the pointer never stops on them.
Tips: If you land on a Bowser Space with no coins but at least one Star, Bowser takes a Star and gives you 10 coins; if you have no coins and no Stars, he gives you 20 coins.

sections.name: Boo
sections.card:
Summary: A ghost that haunts the boards and offers to steal for you: either some coins from a rival at no charge, or a Star at a cost of 50 coins. Every board has a Boo apart from Peach's Birthday Cake.
Tips: On Luigi's Engine Room, whichever way you go, every path finishes at Warp Pipes leading to Boo, who stands close to the start. On Bowser's Magma Mountain, the free roulette at the purple Stone Head can send you to Boo. DK's Jungle Adventure is the only board with two Boos.

sections.name: Whomp (DK's Jungle Adventure)
sections.card:
Summary: A guard on DK's Jungle Adventure that stands at a junction and lets you through only for 10 coins. The board has three.
Weak points: To pass a Whomp on the road it guards, you must pay 10 coins. You can instead take the road it is not watching, but then it shifts over to block the other road once you are through, leaving the first one open to the other three players.
Looks like: Big rectangular stone slabs with jagged-toothed faces and, as with Thwomps, red eyes.
Tips: The Whomp keeps barring that same road for the other players, who must pay as well to get by. A Coin Stone lets a player through only if they hold 20 coins.

sections.name: Thwomps (Yoshi's Tropical Island)
sections.card:
Summary: Two toll guards on the bridges between the two islands of Yoshi's Tropical Island. Each asks a fee to let you cross, starting at 1 coin and rising to a limit of 50.
Weak points: Each Thwomp has its own separate fee, and whoever crosses next has to hand over at least a coin more than the player before. A player who cannot afford the toll is stuck on the island they are on.
Looks like: The Thwomps here use a boxier take on the Super Mario 64 design.
Tips: Landing on a Happening Space has Bubba the fish carry Toad over to the other island while Bowser steps into Toad's spot. Bowser charges 30 coins for a faulty Bowser Tube. Every lap around an island takes you past either Toad or Bowser.

sections.name: Piranha Plant (Peach's Birthday Cake)
sections.card:
Summary: A trap a rival can plant on Peach's Birthday Cake from a Happening Space for 30 coins. It steals a Star from an opponent who lands on its space and gives it to the player who planted it.
Weak points: It does nothing if you have no Stars when you land on it, it disappears once it has taken a Star, and it does nothing to the player who planted it.
Tips: Peach's Birthday Cake has 14 Happening Spaces, and the Strawberry Seed is planted from one of them.

sections.name: Red Space
sections.card:
Summary: A red board space that takes 3 coins from whoever lands on it, or 6 in the last five turns. Every board in the game has some.
Weak points: A Red Space costs the same 3 coins that a Blue Space pays, and both figures double during the final five turns, so each Blue Space stop cancels out one Red Space stop.
Tips: On Bowser's Magma Mountain, landing on a Happening Space makes the volcano erupt and every Blue Space turns red, so the board has 49 Red Spaces instead of 4. The effect starts on the landing player's turn and runs out two turns later, again on that same player's turn.
Tips: Red Spaces per board: DK's Jungle Adventure 7, Yoshi's Tropical Island 3, Peach's Birthday Cake 4, Wario's Battle Canyon 7, Luigi's Engine Room 4, Mario's Rainbow Castle 5, Bowser's Magma Mountain 4 and Eternal Star 3.

sections.name: Rolling boulder (DK's Jungle Adventure)
sections.card:
Summary: A boulder that a Happening Space sets rolling on DK's Jungle Adventure. It sends any player in its way back toward the start.
Weak points: It only hits players caught in front of it as it rolls down Bowser's path, and a player it sweeps back still lands on a Blue Space and gets its three coins.
Tips: The board has nine Happening Spaces. When the game ends, the boulder chases whoever came fourth down the board.

sections.name: Pisudon (Luigi's Engine Room)
sections.card:
Summary: A robot on Luigi's Engine Room that will switch the board's doors for 20 coins. Two of them are on the board.
Weak points: A Pisudon offers the switch when a player crosses paths with it, and the switch blocks access to certain paths for the other players.

sections.name: Bowser's bogus items
sections.card:
Summary: Useless things Bowser makes you buy when you walk by him on a board, a different one on each of six boards, for 10 to 40 coins.
Uses: None of them helps you. The Gold-plated Bowser Statue is 10 coins on DK's Jungle Adventure, the Bowser Cake 20 on Peach's Birthday Cake, the Bowser Tube 30 on Yoshi's Tropical Island, Bowser's Claws or Cannon 20 on Wario's Battle Canyon, the Make As Many Coins As You Want Mecha 20 on Luigi's Engine Room, and the Ztar 40 on Mario's Rainbow Castle.
Looks like: The Gold-plated Bowser Statue is a small model of the Koopa King, the Bowser Cake is a spiked shell topped by a candle and some frosting, and the Ztar is a black star with white eyes.
Tips: Bowser's Claws shoot you off to a random place on the board. The price is 20 coins, or all of yours if you hold 20 or fewer, and nothing if you hold none. The Make As Many Coins As You Want Mecha hands back one coin for the 20 you pay, so you are down 19.
Tips: Straight after you "buy" the Ztar you walk by Koopa Troopa and get 10 coins back. That rises to 20 in the final five turns or when it is the tenth time anyone has gone by him, to 30 on the twentieth time, and onward. On Bowser's Magma Mountain and Eternal Star he sells nothing; he takes a Star instead, or else up to 20 coins from a player who has no Star.

sections.name: Event Block
sections.card:
Summary: A 200-coin Mushroom Shop item that hides a visit from Bowser, Koopa Troopa or Boo on one space of the board.
Uses: When a player lands on the hidden space, Koopa Troopa drops in and hands them 20 coins; Boo does his usual theft of coins or a Star; or Bowser takes 20 coins, or whatever they have if it is less, and gives a single coin to a player with none.
Tips: Once bought, you can switch it on or off at the bank. Bowser's coin is wiped out when the player is on a Red Space.

sections.name: Coin Box, Lucky Box and Casino Box
sections.card:
Summary: Three boxes that keep your coins and Stars safe once a board game is over: the Coin Box you are given first, the 400-coin Lucky Box and the 300-coin Casino Box.
Uses: The Lucky Box gives you an extra 10% of each round's coin total. After every game the Casino Box spins a roulette: x2 doubles the coins you put in, -1/2 throws out half of them, and 0 changes nothing.
Tips: The Casino Box has a cap of 100 Stars and 99,999 coins. At the Mushroom Bank, Porto is where you pick which to save with: the Casino Box, Lucky Box or Coin Box.
Tips: Storing at the game's end happens for human-controlled players only.

sections.name: No Koopa and No Boo
sections.card:
Summary: Two 500-coin Mushroom Shop items, one named for Koopa Troopa and one for Boo.
Uses: While No Koopa is active, Koopa Troopa does not hand you the 10 coins for passing the starting point.
Tips: You must finish the Eternal Star map before either item can be bought.

sections.name: Mushroom Space (Mushroom and Poisonous Mushroom)
sections.card:
Summary: A board space that spins a roulette between a Mushroom, which gives you another roll, and a Poisonous Mushroom, which costs you your next turn.
Uses: The Mushroom lets you roll again. The Poisonous Mushroom costs you your next turn.
Tips: You cannot steer the outcome by timing your jump, because it is settled as soon as you land.
Tips: Mushroom Spaces per board: DK's Jungle Adventure 3, Yoshi's Tropical Island 3, Peach's Birthday Cake 6, Wario's Battle Canyon 5, Luigi's Engine Room 3, Mario's Rainbow Castle 2, Bowser's Magma Mountain 3 and Eternal Star 3.

sections.name: Chance Time Space (the ! Space)
sections.card:
Summary: A rare board space marked with an exclamation mark that starts Chance Time, where three Dice Blocks decide who gives what to whom.
Uses: The middle block can make one player give 10, 20 or 30 coins or 1 Star to the other, and two more results, marked with a double arrow, swap all coins or all Stars.
Tips: You can roll the three blocks in whatever order you like. Once you choose a character on one side, that character is gone from the other side, and each roll makes the blocks go faster. In the first game a ! Space counts as a Blue Space, and where the Star relocates after someone buys it, the ! Space is put on the spot the Star last stood on.
Tips: Bowser's Chance Time, one of the Bowser Space events, is rigged: from the start the blocks whirl too fast to control, Bowser is locked in on the right block, and a loser with nothing gets 10 coins from Bowser, out of pity.

sections.name: Gameballs, Mecha Fly Guy, Talking Parrot and Record
sections.card:
Summary: Four of the Mushroom Shop's items, priced 50 to 300 coins: Gameballs, the Mecha Fly Guy, the Talking Parrot and the Record.
Uses: Gameballs cost 300 coins and the Mecha Fly Guy costs 100. The Mecha Fly Guy belongs to the Mini-Game House.
Tips: Gameballs turn up in the shop once you have bought 30 or more mini-games at the Mini-Game House, and stay usable until every mini-game there is bought.
Tips: The Record, at 50 coins, is what unlocks the Option House's Juke Box, and only for songs you have already heard in the game. The 50-coin Talking Parrot plays random character voices there when you press its button.
